steps.label: Where and when they are formed
steps.margin_note: Two columns or paired lines. Keep the same order in every pair.
lines: Formed on the bark of woody stems and woody
Formed on the leaves and on younger green
steps.why: A lenticel is a break in the cork, so it can only exist where cork exists, which is on a woody part after secondary growth. A stoma is a gap in the epidermis, so it exists where the epidermis is still present.
common_mistakes: Writing that lenticels occur on leaves. Leaves have stomata, not lenticels.
Missing the stage of growth. Secondary against primary is a marked difference.
steps.memory_tip: Cork carries lenticels; epidermis carries stomata.

steps.label: The opening and the guard cells
steps.margin_note: Two marks here. Both the shape of the opening and the guard cells are needed.
lines: The opening is lens shaped and comparatively
It is not surrounded by guard cells, so it
The opening, called the stomatal pore, is
It is surrounded by two guard cells, which
steps.why: Whether the pore can close is the real difference between the two. Guard cells change shape with their water content, and a lenticel has no such cells, so it cannot be shut.
common_mistakes: Saying a lenticel has guard cells. It has none.
Forgetting that the number of guard cells at a stoma is two.
steps.memory_tip: Lens shaped and always open is a lenticel; narrow and closable is a stoma.

steps.label: Complementary cells
steps.margin_note: End with the one-line contrast so the table has a conclusion.
lines: Complementary cells are present. They are
loosely arranged cells that fill the lenticel
and leave spaces between them for gases to

lines.text: Both exchange gases; only the stoma can close

steps.why: A lenticel still has to keep water in while letting gases through, and the loose complementary cells do this without having to open or close, which is why no guard cells are needed.
common_mistakes: Mixing up complementary cells with subsidiary cells. Subsidiary cells belong to a stoma.
Writing that complementary cells close the lenticel. They do not move.
steps.memory_tip: Complementary cells belong to the lenticel; subsidiary cells belong to the stoma.

insider_note: Both are gas-exchange openings, so the examiner wants the differences listed in matched pairs, not two separate descriptions.
